findings.label: ShareComposer selected/unselected icon collision
findings.detail: In dark, SHARE_COMPOSER.dark.unselectedIcon (DARK_TONAL.violet.fg) and the selected t.color.primaryFg are both #c4a3ff, so the muted-vs-emphasised recipient ring is lost. Selection is still shown by glyph and card stripe. This is rule-1a/3-correct but against the light intent. Raise it at the screenshot/integration step: use a muted dark value (e.g. darkColor.textSecondary/borderStrong) as a recorded design exception and add a dark assertion.

findings.label: ParkWaitPulse active ring nearly invisible in dark
findings.detail: activeBorder -> DARK_TONAL.green.border #2e5150 with activeShadow #000000 is barely stronger than the inactive violet.border #584678. Confirm with a screenshot (the coder flagged it). If confirmed, treat the state ring as role T (green.fg) by design exception.

findings.label: Typecheck/related-tests evidence is scoped
findings.detail: C5 was a TS-API check of the 68 B6 files (0 diagnostics) because B7's ChangePasswordControl.tsx syntax error blocks root tsc. C6 had 10 suites fail to load on B4/B5/B7 in-flight files, so the navigation/friends/notificationNavigation suites never ran against B6. Integration must run the full npm run verify.

findings.label: Share/Attribution dark values untested
findings.detail: InboxScreen, SentSharesScreen, ShareComposerScreen and AttributionScreen have no dark render assertions (accepted by the plan). Screenshots for these screens matter, since B6-1 is exactly the kind of defect this gap lets through.
